reviewer: Codex primary final critical reading; selected separate-reader findings retained in evidence/reviews. No human/Claude acceptance claimed.

clarity.evidence: A product record and a slow stale read explain the stale-fill race before cache topology.

scope.evidence: Chosen distributed architecture is explained separately from the complete bounded single-node Java mechanism.

contracts.evidence: Generation/version tickets, slot incarnation, original age budget and product database authority agree across diagrams and code.

correctness.evidence: CacheChecks covers delayed fill, TTL equality, byte/slot bounds, ABA retirement, defensive copies, nanoTime wrap and 32 invalidations.

failure_handling.evidence: Invalidation fences delayed loads; eviction creates a new incarnation so an old ticket cannot overwrite a replacement; cache loss falls back under bounded admission.

tradeoffs.evidence: Consistent routing, L1 freshness, asynchronous replicas, LRU and hot-key/stampede protection have stated costs and unimplemented distributed boundaries.

visual_learning.evidence: Three executable histories show current value, rejected stale fill and eviction/recreation; a text sequence accompanies the controls.

code.evidence: examples/learning-java/src/kb/cache; full copyable source/download parity and exact excerpts checked by check_review_lot.py; actual runtime output in lot-command-output.json and lot-runtime.json.

rendering.evidence: HLD-3-browser.json: article and walkthrough in light/dark at 1280/390px; theme controls, navigation, no missing images/page-wide overflow, table contrast >=4.5. Per-topic assets resolve.

limits: Local mechanism and fixture checks do not establish remote-provider behavior, distributed durability/failover, production throughput or model quality. Scope-specific boundaries are explicit in the answer.
